title: The Rise and Fall of D.O.D.O.

description.main: A time-travel novel by Neal Stephenson and Nicole Galland about a secret government agency that tries to change history with magic.
description.extended:
The Rise and Fall of D.O.D.O. is a time-travel novel by Neal Stephenson and Nicole Galland, built around a secret U.S. government agency that tries to change history through magic.

The agency is the Department of Diachronic Operations, which gives the book its title. The story is set mainly in the present-day United States, and the agency sends its operatives into historical periods that include London in 1601, Constantinople in 1203 and 1204, and London in 1851. William Morrow published the hardcover on June 13, 2017, at 768 pages, and it entered the New York Times hardcover fiction list at number 11.

Stephenson and Galland had already written together on The Mongoliad, the shared-authorship serial published in three volumes in 2012 and 2013. Stephenson returned to solo novels with Fall; or, Dodge in Hell (2019).

notes: First US hardcover edition (William Morrow, 2017), written with Nicole Galland. Book one of the D.O.D.O. series.
